**MR af tyndtarmen** (MRI of the small intestine) is an advanced diagnostic imaging procedure that forms a critical part of the clinical workup program for newly diagnosed children and young people with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in Denmark [^src1]. 

The procedure's utilization is monitored as part of the Danish IBD registry (DANIBD), which evaluates the quality of care across the country. In the second annual report covering the period from October 1, 2023, to September 30, 2024, the registry analyzed data from 751 pediatric and youth patients alongside 33,599 adults [^src1]. While the report highlights various aspects of clinical practice, the steering committee (Styregruppen for DANIBD) specifically problematizes the underutilization of this imaging technique [^src1]. According to their findings, MR af tyndtarmen is not performed in 31% of the relevant cases where it is indicated, pointing to a significant gap in the diagnostic scope for young IBD patients [^src1]. This missing application is noted alongside broader systemic challenges regarding clinical coding and preventive interventions identified by the committee and the Danish Healthcare Quality Programme (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut) [^src1].
